sentences.span: Yesterday President Trump confirmed that he rejected Iran's proposal for a 7 day ceasefire
sentences.why: The rejection is real but happened Friday/Saturday (both 17998, dated Sun 27 Sep 12:38pm ET, and 17989, 'On Friday after the close, Trump announced that he had rejected Iran's proposal') — no source shows a fresh rejection 'again this morning.' The sentence asserts a same-day repeat event that isn't in the corpus.

sentences.span: Both a de-escalation in the Gulf & the (safe) passage past the Mid-Terms are required before re-risking
sentences.why: Multiple sources (GS Wilson, 17991 'Short-term direction hinges on Iran de-escalation') show markets conditioned on de-escalation; with the ceasefire rejected and oil/yields pushing higher, the escalation case is what's printing instead. Framing-level synthesis, not a specific figure — no contradiction found.

sentences.span: Strait of Hormuz flows are hovering at ~13-14 million barrels a day (7-day average). That's about the same as the brief peak in July.
sentences.why: No source states Hormuz flows at 'roughly a quarter of normal' — the only Hormuz flow-rate data found (17989, citing Javier Blas/Bloomberg) puts flows near the July peak, not a quarter of it. Separately, most inflation sources in the corpus (17848, 18023, 17928) show core inflation holding stable/moderating even as energy prices rise, contradicting 'hitting core inflation as much as...pump prices.'

sentences.span: Saudi crude exports via Hormuz were on track to rebound to 3.6 million barrels per day in September, up from about 900,000 bpd in August
sentences.why: 3.6M/0.9M is exactly a ~4x ('quadrupling') increase off August's low. The $150/bbl escalation threshold is directly supported by 18006 ('Brent prices could rise well beyond current levels and potentially exceed $150/bbl') and corroborated by 17878 and 17906/17907's 120-150/bbl range.

sentences.span: NO DEAL WITH ESCALATION – a return to $100/bbl oil and the 10Y yield above 5% is the assumption here
sentences.why: JPMorgan's framework has three scenarios (DEAL / NO DEAL BUT NO ESCALATION / NO DEAL WITH ESCALATION); oil-near-$100/10Y-above-5% belongs specifically to the escalation sub-case, not to 'the no-deal case' generally, so collapsing it into a single 'no-deal case' misattributes which scenario is printing. Separately, no source in the corpus supports 'Saudi Arabia's foreign minister meeting Rubio in Washington' — searched found only unrelated Rubio mentions (G20/Venezuela, PRC-hawk commentary).

sentences.span: After hitting an intra-day high of $108.16/bbl Brent crude did see a mostly temporary drop of around $4
sentences.why: Brent touched $108.16 intraday then pulled back roughly $4; the same doc's data box shows Brent closing at $105.61. 'Holding above $108' overstates a brief intraday spike as a sustained level — no source shows Brent holding above $108.

sentences.span: The 10-year has broken out of a three-year range, MOVE has surged, and small caps are feeling the pressure
sentences.why: Directly matches the breakout claim; MOVE's sharp two-session jump is separately confirmed in 17870 ('MOVE Index has jumped 33% past 2 days'), and 17862 independently glosses MOVE as 'the bond market's version of the VIX.'

No source document can attest to what 'this pulse' called on September 22 — that is a claim about the pulse's own prior edition, not something any of the day's research PDFs would contain. The 5.2%/5.5% levels themselves are corroborated elsewhere (17908: 'Watch the 5.2% area first. Beyond that, the next major level is 5.5%'), but the sentence's load-bearing claim — the prior call and 'got there' framing — has zero source support in this corpus.

sentences.span: Batteries - Framing the battery backup unit opportunity, $50bn by 2030 (CAGR +87%); Buy Panasonic HD
sentences.why: The $50bn battery figure is real but comes from a separate GS note on Panasonic HD, unconnected to the DC-power-systems forecast (which is ABB's, from 17743: 'ABB expects 25-40% of new datacenter additions in 2030 to be based on [DC]'). The sentence attributes both to a single 'it,' implying one company's DC shift opens the $50bn battery market — that causal link isn't in either source.
Goldman's Exhibit 1 confirms all five names (META, GOOGL, AMZN, V, MA) as Buy-rated within the agentic-commerce/toll thesis, with META PT $725 and AMZN PT $375 matching exactly.

sentences.span: hyperscaler-funded data centers risk becoming the most capital-destructive stranded assets in the history of technology ... Are the four hyperscalers really going to spend US$990bn on capex in 2027 ... GREED & fear severely doubts it
sentences.why: Jefferies (Chris Wood's Greed & Fear) is explicitly and strongly skeptical of AI capex paying off, doubting the $990bn 2027 consensus estimate and warning of 'capital-destructive stranded assets' — a fair gloss of a capex-vs-return skepticism, even though the exact phrase 'return on equity' isn't used here.

Attributed to Goldman's actual Buy ratings and price targets on META/AMZN under the toll thesis; watching earnings vs. targets is a reasonable framing of an actual analyst call, not an invented house position.

sentences.span: The S&P 500 is near its highs, but only about a quarter of its stocks are above their 50-day averages
sentences.why: Directly matches; corroborated by 17998 ('median stock in the index trades 16% below its 52-week high, dragging market breadth to its lowest level since the Dot-Com Bubble').

sentences.span: investors are likely to scrutinise whether outsized capital expenditure is translating into sustainable return on equity
sentences.why: Direct match to Eastspring's (CIO Views bulletin author) stated question, correctly attributed.

sentences.span: investors are paying an above-average P/E premium for 3-year ahead sales growth
sentences.why: Closing synthesis line consistent with multiple sources in the set (P/E premium for growth, deteriorating breadth, Eastspring's ROE question) without asserting a specific figure or attribution that could be checked and found wrong.
